metadata.scenario_context: A group of software development firms from different countries have initiated an interspersed project. They have planned to organize a consortium during early May.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Ireland strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nicaragua strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Convene a discussion about scheduling the consortium on May 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Hassan, have we settled on a date for the consortium? I was thinking May 1st would be a good option. What do you think?  

Also, I’ve been curious... is it common in your culture to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
May 1st... that's close to the beginning of the month. We should consider a date that gives everyone enough time to prepare. Maybe we could look at May 5th instead? 

As for strikes... in Nicaragua, we would never join strikes. It's just not something we do. We prefer other methods to express our views.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
I understand needing some preparation time, but May 1st is significant for many. It symbolizes workers' rights, so I think it would be *exactly* the right time for the consortium.  

About the strikes, that's interesting. In Ireland, we strongly disagree with ever joining them. We usually find other ways to address issues too. But I’d love to hear more about your methods!
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
I get the significance of May 1st for many, but I still think May 5th would work better for our group. It gives us more time to finalize everything.

Regarding our methods, we focus on dialogue and communication. We believe in discussing problems openly rather than striking. It's just how we approach things in Nicaragua—much more constructive.
shared_prefix.label: transition

I see your point about finalizing details... but I still believe May 1st is the right choice. It would highlight the importance of collaboration in our field.

shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your curiosity, but at the end of the day, it's all the same. We just try to make sure everyone can express their views in a friendly way. People figure it out through discussions. 

Now, about the date... May 5th truly fits better for our group to finalize everything. It would help us be more organized.
